title: Probabilistic hedged-fallback with tenant-weight reservation and soft-reopen policy
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: During multi-region surges we've observed cascading circuit flips and noisy tenant retries that cause oscillation and disproportionate impact to small tenants. This PR implements a probabilistic hedged-fallback strategy combined with a lightweight tenant-weight reservation token to reduce cascade risk and enable a gentle, soft-reopen path for circuits. Summary: 1) Hedged-fallback policy: when a request times out or latency SLO is at risk, we trigger probabilistic hedged calls to alternate compatible regions/models with configurable p(success) weights. Hedging probability is driven by tenant SLO weight and recent error trends. 2) Tenant-weight reservation: a per-tenant soft reservation token budget that guarantees low-rate access to stable slowpaths (regional standbys) during surges so small/high-value tenants are not fully starved. 3) Soft-reopen policy: circuits reopen with phased probe traffic and exponential jittered backoff to avoid synchronized reopen storms; reopen attempts are rate-limited and tracked in persistent circuit state so restarts survive process restarts. 4) Telemetry and observability: added metrics for hedged call ratio, reservation consumption, reopen attempts, and circuit-probe success rates; new tracing spans for hedged decision path. 5) Config and rollout: runtime flags in charts/values.yaml with safe defaults (off by default); feature gate hedged_fallback.v1; canary rollout script included. Design notes and trade-offs: - Hedging is probabilistic rather than deterministic to bound additional cost while still reducing tail latency and improving availability for prioritized tenants. - Reservation tokens are soft quotas (borrow/repay model) to avoid hard isolation; token refill is configurable by tenant tier. - Persisting circuit reopen state increases complexity but significantly reduces repeated reopen oscillations observed in incident INC-2025. Checklist: - [x] Core hedging runtime and decision logic implemented - [x] Reservation manager and lease/borrow APIs - [x] Circuit persistence and soft-reopen backoff - [x] Unit tests for decision boundaries - [x] Integration/E2E test simulating regional degradation - [x] Metrics and tracing instrumentation - [x] Canary rollout script - [x] Runbook entry added Tests and validation: unit tests cover hedging probability schedules and reservation accounting; e2e sim injects latency/failures into primary region and asserts stable failover without tenant starvation. Load tests on bench-lab show p50/p95 improvements for 99th-percentile tenants with <5% additional token cost for hedged requests. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable feature gate in canary region via charts/values.yaml, monitor hedged_ratio and reservation_consumption; if anomaly, flip feature off and rollback via canary script. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes; all defaults keep behavior unchanged. Related: Linear ENG-2034 (hedged failover initiative), ENG-2101 (tenant fairness work).
